problem:
By changing the order of integration in the following repeated integrals so that they are integrated first with respect to $x,$ then $y,$ and then $z,$ express the following sum as a single repeated integral.

$$
{\int }_{-2}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{y+2}}{\int }_{-z}^{{y}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{2}^{6}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{6-y}}{\int }_{-z}^{{y}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y
$$

activity_context.topic_title: Changing the Order of Integration in Triple Integrals: Changing Projection

feedback.problem:
By changing the order of integration, find the missing limits in the following repeated integral.

$$
{\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{({x}^{2}-4)/2}^{(x+2)^{3}/4}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x={\int }_{p}^{0}{\int }_{q}^{0}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{r}^{0}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{{v}_{3}(y)}^{{v}_{4}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{3}(x,y)}^{{u}_{4}(x,y)}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,-2\le x\le 0,\,\,\frac{1}{2}({x}^{2}-4)\le y\le \frac{1}{4}(x+2)^{3},\,\,x\le z\le {y}^{2}}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{({x}^{2}-4)/2}^{(x+2)^{3}/4}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{{v}_{3}(y)}^{{v}_{4}(y)}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/a38afc63496b487803590ccd57e2ab92ad4061524007e8bb4fb6277ff952dde2.png)

The region $D$ is a type I region in the $xz$-plane:

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,-2\le x\le 0,\,\frac{1}{2}({x}^{2}-4)\le y\le \frac{1}{4}(x+2)^{3}}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y,$ we split $D$ into two type II regions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/9bbaf6d9ce11ecbd988954365e9693f7f3f175c1dd0f944cc85b73773beca047.png)

Notice that the bottom and top boundaries of the lower region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ are

$\,$ $x=-\sqrt{2y+4}\,$ and $\,x=0.$

Also, the bottom and top boundaries of the upper region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ are

$\,$ $x=\sqrt[3]{4y}-2\,$ and $\,x=0.$

So, we can write $D$ as a union of

$$
{D}_{1}={(x,y)\,:\,-2\le y\le 0,\,-\sqrt{2y+4}\le x\le 0}
$$

and

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,\sqrt[3]{4y}-2\le x\le 0}.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{-\sqrt{2y+4}}^{0}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{\sqrt[3]{4y}-2}^{0}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$
